plan.topic: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure? A new meta-regression of Phase 3 trials of GLP-1 and multi-hormone drugs in adults with overweight or obesity (EClinicalMedicine, Oct 12, 2026)
plan.angle: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure? In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, 72 weeks), systolic blood pressure fell more on tirzepatide than on placebo. Quote the exact NEJM mmHg figures. Then the bigger picture: a pooled analysis of 32 Phase 3 obesity-drug trials found blood pressure fell more where weight fell more (about 0.34 mmHg per 1% of weight lost). That's 'linked to', pooled data, not head-to-head, and blood pressure wasn't the trials' main goal. Cite it by its verified publication (otherwise as the ECO May 2026 analysis). Add 'Never change your blood pressure medicines on your own; review lower readings with your doctor', one GI line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Does Tirzepatide Lower Blood Pressure? New Trial Analysis
plan.why: Tirzepatide-first titles are our proven Shorts format (median 102). This is a fresh peer-reviewed meta-regression on a searched beyond-weight question, with little video coverage. | fact-check: I couldn't confirm an EClinicalMedicine paper dated 12 Oct 2026. The only version I could verify is the European Congress on Obesity abstract (EurekAlert, 14 May 2026): 32 Phase 3 trials, 43,618 adults with overweight or obesity, a pooled −10.9% placebo-adjusted weight loss and −5.2 mmHg systolic, and about 0.34 mmHg less systolic pressure per 1% of weight lost. It gives NO figure for tirzepatide alone. Its stated caveat: blood pressure wasn't a primary outcome, and changes to background blood pressure medicines may have affected the results. So the tirzepatide answer has to come from SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022, week 72, versus placebo, population without diabetes). Copy that figure exactly from the paper. Cite the meta-analysis only by its confirmed published record (journal, date, DOI). If the scriptwriter can't find it, call it the 'May 2026 European Congress on Obesity analysis'. Add a safety line: people on blood pressure medicines can get readings that run low; discuss it with your doctor. Source: https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1128310

package.title: Does Tirzepatide Lower Blood Pressure? What Trials Show #shorts
package.description:
In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with overweight/obesity, no diabetes), tirzepatide (all doses combined) lowered systolic blood pressure 7.2 mmHg vs 1.0 mmHg with placebo over 72 weeks. A May 2026 pooled analysis of 32 Phase 3 obesity-drug trials linked each 1% of weight lost to about 0.34 mmHg lower systolic pressure—pooled data, not head-to-head, and blood pressure wasn't the main goal. Most common side effects: nausea, diarrhea. If you're on blood pressure medicine, don't change it on your own—review lower readings with your doctor.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

That moment the blood pressure cuff tightens and you brace for the number? You're not alone: nearly half of US adults have high blood pressure.

So does tirzepatide move that number?

In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with overweight or obesity, no diabetes; 1,896 on tirzepatide, 643 on placebo, 72 weeks), systolic blood pressure—the top number—fell 7.2 mmHg on tirzepatide (all doses combined) vs 1.0 mmHg on placebo.

If you're on blood pressure medicine already, readings may trend lower—never adjust your meds on your own. Bring any lower readings to your doctor. Most common side effects of tirzepatide: nausea and diarrhea.

factcheck.summary:
The script is accurate and safe, and it can ship. Two optional wording fixes are listed below.

**Checked against sources:**
- **CDC (s2):** confirmed. The page says "Nearly half of adults have high blood pressure (48.1%, 119.9 million)", from 2017 to March 2020 survey data.
- **ECO 2026 news release, 14 May 2026 (s5, s6):** confirmed. It covers 32 Phase 3 trials with 43,618 adults with overweight or obesity, and systolic pressure about 0.34 mmHg lower per 1% of weight lost. It also gives the caveats the script uses: blood pressure was not the main outcome, changes to blood pressure medicines may have played a part, and the analysis pooled whole-trial results.

**Checked from memory (the journal blocked access):**
- The SURMOUNT-1 group sizes (1,896 on tirzepatide across all doses, 643 on placebo) and the 72 weeks are correct.
- The −7.2 versus −1.0 mmHg systolic change at week 72 (all doses combined) matches the published paper as I know it. I couldn't open the journal page to see it directly. A separate SURMOUNT-1 analysis found blood pressure fell meaningfully more on tirzepatide than placebo, which fits.
- Nausea and diarrhea are correctly named as the most common side effects.

**Framing and safety are good:**
- The pooled result is worded as "linked to", not "causes".
- It says the trials weren't compared directly and that blood pressure wasn't the main goal.
- It tells viewers not to change blood pressure medicines on their own.
- The disclaimer and the prescriber line are there, and the call to action doesn't name a video it can't link to.
- The narration is about 150 words, under the 170-word limit.

Coming straight after the tirzepatide trial, viewers could take the 32 trials as tirzepatide trials. It is also a conference presentation, not yet a published journal paper.

audio.soundNotes: Music was already sitting right in the -12 to -15 dB window, so left the overall level untouched. Fixed two real problems: a near-unmasked swoosh at 7.6s (-5.8 dB, right on top of speech) and a pair of effects at 42.5s that measured almost silent (-33 dB) despite high set gain; boosted them to the 1.5x cap (as close to the -14/-20 target as the cap allows) and added a quick custom chime accent there so the "32 Phase 3 trials" reveal still lands audibly. Also trimmed a cluster of 6+ simultaneous chip-pop sounds at 19–20s and a 7-deep stack at the −7.2 vs −1.0 stat reveal (31.8–32.9s) down to 3–4 clean hits each. Thinned the SFX right at "Never change them alone" to keep that safety line serious and uncluttered, and added bespoke on-theme blood-pressure sounds (cuff hiss at the open, soft heartbeats under the systolic stat, one deep pulse under the safety line) for a distinct sonic identity that never competes with the narrator.
